I'm trying to install the Google Nest doorbell (3rd generation), and I'm having a really hard time getting the doorbell to sit flush with the mounting bracket.

Additionally, all the fiddling around has led to one of the wires breaking off (they're 25+ years old). I exposed new wire, but there isn't that much left anymore, and if it breaks again, I fear having to re-wire the whole thing.

As it stands, the doorbell is mounted to the bracket and is fastened using the security screw on top. It's pretty stable and likely won't go anywhere, but there is a gap at the bottom, and I fear water/snow can cause damage to the doorbell (and wires?) in the long run.

My suspicion for the doorbell not sitting flush is that the wires are getting in the way. To fix this, I was thinking of using heat shrink butt connectors to extend the wires. Once extended, I'd tuck away the bulky part (the jacket and connectors) inside the hole and only leave the thinner wires outside.

Is there a better way?

Should I just leave it as is? If the wires and doorbell won't get damaged due to the gap at the bottom, I'd be open to this option.

I think I cut too much of my ceiling when installing a new ceiling fan, hoping to get advice on where to go from here.
I bought a Hampton Bay Glendale III to replace my old ceiling fan. Once I removed the old fan, I tried to install the mounting bracket but found that the outlet box was a little too deep inside the ceiling for my mounting screws to reach. When I placed the mounting bracket flush against the ceiling, the screws were unable to reach the outlet box. I think this is where I messed up; I considered getting longer screws but decided instead to cut the outline of the mounting bracket into the ceiling dry wall to get the mounting bracket to press against the outlet box and enable the screws to fasten them together.

Later, I found that due to getting the mounting bracket pressed up against the outlet box inside the ceiling, the canopy could not fasten against the mounting bracket. The only way the canopy could reach the mounting bracket right now would be to cut even more dry wall out, which probably wouldn't do. What should I do from here? Fix enough of the drywall to install the mounting bracket flush against the ceiling? Buy a larger canopy so it doesn't have to go into the ceiling? Or something else entirely?
Thank you!
